panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the primary lesion on the left thenar eminence in a patient whose biopsy was diagnostic of clear cell acanthoma; the solitary erythematous papule/nodule is a recognized clinical manifestation of CCA. B: Low-power H&E of the diagnostic shave biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia composed of pale-staining keratinocytes, the classic histologic pattern of clear cell acanthoma attributed in the caption and text to CCA. C: Higher-power H&E demonstrating the sharp demarcation between the pale-celled epidermal tumor and adjacent normal epidermis, a characteristic histologic feature of clear cell acanthoma explicitly captioned in this CCA case.
panels.attribution_text: Melson et al. Clear Cell Acanthoma with Malignant Cytologic Features: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.. Dermatopathology (Basel, Switzerland) 2022. doi:10.3390/dermatopathology9040041. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Clinical image of the initial left thenar eminence lesion, prior to shave biopsy. (B) Low power examination of the initial shave biopsy specimen revealed an epidermal tumor exhibiting psoriasiform hyperplasia composed of pale staining cells (H&E, 20×) with (C) an abrupt transition to the adjacent normal epidermis at one lateral edge (H&E, 100×).
in_text_mentions: A 78-year-old male with prior history of immune thrombocytopenia and multiple nonmelanoma skin cancers presented to dermatology clinic with a new growth on the thenar eminence of the left palm (Figure 1A) measuring 1.0 cm × 0.8 cm. He reported it had been present for several weeks and was occasionally painful. It persisted after treatment with liquid nitrogen. At his next visit, a tangential biopsy was performed. Histopathology showed marked epidermal hyperplasia with areas of well-demarcated pallor and mild spongiosis consistent with CCA (Figure 1B,C).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a well-delimited, shiny erythematous plaque on the left buttock in a 73-year-old woman; the article title ('Hidden clear cell acanthoma with uncommon dermoscopic findings') and in-text description attribute this lesion to clear cell acanthoma, and the caption describes the classic clinical manifestation (erythematous shiny plaque).
panels.attribution_text: Álvarez-Salafranca et al. Hidden clear cell acanthoma with uncommon dermoscopic findings.. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2021. doi:10.1016/j.abd.2020.06.027. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Well delimited erythematous shiny plaque on the left buttock, surrounded by a hypopigmented area.
in_text_mentions: A 73-year-old woman presented with less than a 1-year history of an erythematous, well-delimited and shiny lesion on her left buttock, near the gluteal fold (Fig. 1). Dermoscopic examination showed dotted vessels arranged in a linear pattern involving the entire lesion. These vascular findings are also called metaphorically a ‘string of pearls’ pattern. Another vascular pattern observed on the periphery of the lesion is that of branched vessels with rounded endings. panels.rationale: Single H&E histology panel from a case report of HPV-positive giant clear cell acanthoma. Caption describes intracytoplasmic glycogen and intraepidermal microabscesses; image shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia. Included as real patient histology of the configured target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Cuomo et al. Human Papillomavirus-Associated Giant Clear Cell Acanthoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Rare Case Report and Literature Review.. Journal of clinical medicine 2024. doi:10.3390/jcm13092482. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological evaluation of the lesion with an accumulation of intracytoplasmic glycogen and a predominant presence of eosinophilic granulocytes within intraepidermal micro-abscesses; Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated positivity for p16 indicative of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
in_text_mentions: atures included dyskeratosis and coilocytotic-like changes. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated positivity for p16, which is a marker often associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection (Figure 4). These findings led to a diagnosis of HPV-positive clear cell acanthoma in conjunction with keratinised squamous cell carcinoma. Additionally, a melanocytic nevus exhibiting severe atypia was identified within the lesion’s composition.
